title: Token-lease TTL misalignment causing reserved-pool burst denials — incident, hotfix, and follow-up
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: On 2026-01-22 morning US-PST, multiple customers (notably: Centauri Payments and BeaconHealth) observed sustained 'burst capacity denied' errors while their reserved pools showed available headroom. Traffic spikes coincided with these errors which produced request-level failures and escalations to Support and SE. Impact: short-lived denials for burst requests (5-15s windows) that resulted in request retries, elevated tail latency for chat requests, and degraded SLAs for VIP tenants for ~2.5 hours. Root cause: a TTL misalignment between the allocator's token-lease expiry and the burst-credit-reconciler/eviction controller. The allocator issued ephemeral request leases with a 6s TTL; the reconciler assumed a 30s lease window when calculating available burst headroom and when reassigning released slots. Under load, race conditions caused lease expirations between token handoff and KV-cache warmup, so slot accounting briefly reported less available capacity. The autoscaler and routing logic interpreted transient low-utilization signals (caused by those expirations) as insufficient warmup and suppressed scale-ups due to a conservative hysteresis circuit. Net effect: available physical capacity remained but was not admitted for burst traffic during TTL jitter windows, causing denial spikes.

Timeline and detection: 2026-01-22 09:12 UTC - first customer escalation from SE. 09:18 UTC - on-call triaged networking vs. GPU OOM; initial infra checks green. 09:28 UTC - Grafana histograms showed a spike in 'lease_expire_before_activation' and simultaneous drop in 'admitted_burst_slots'. 09:35 UTC - reproduce in staging with synthetic 1000qps microburst; observed identical denial pattern when allocator TTL < reconciler safety window. 09:49 UTC - emergency mitigation deployed: allocator TTL increased to 45s and a short-term conservative lease-renewal introduced. 10:05 UTC - customer-facing mitigation message and escalations updates. 11:30 UTC - hotfix PR merged (allocator TTL logic + reconciliation guard) and rolled out to US regions. 12:55 UTC - monitoring showed denials return to baseline. Post-incident follow-up concluded 2026-02-05.

Immediate mitigations taken: 1) Increased allocator token-lease TTL to 45s to remove race window. 2) Introduced a lease-renewal handshake for in-flight warmups: allocator now attempts a single 15s renewal if activation not observed. 3) Temporarily relaxed autoscaler hysteresis for reserved-pool admission signals in impacted AZs to allow proactive scale-ups while telemetry stabilized. 4) Proactively warmed selected VIP tenants in the impacted pools to drain queues.

Permanent fixes delivered in runtime-1.24.3: - Deterministic TTL alignment between allocator and reconciler (single source-of-truth TTL config). - Guard logic in reconciler to ignore transient lease expiries if activation trace exists within 60s. - Autoscaler tuning: updated signal fusion to weigh lease-expire and activation latency separately so short-lived expiries don't veto scale-ups. - Added unit+integration tests around lease lifecycle and a new chaos test that randomly drops lease-acquire confirmations.

Postmortem and actions: - Observability: Created new metrics: lease_acquire_latency, lease_renewal_count, lease_expire_before_activation; dashboards added to Console under 'Reserved Pool Health'. - Runbook: Added a dedicated playbook section for "Lease TTL drift / Burst denial" with triage steps and recommended emergency mitigations. - Reliability engineering: Implemented a nightly synthetic microburst job that validates admission across AZs and flags TTL mismatches. - Policy: Configured canary rollout for TTL changes with automatic rollback on >1% denial regression. - Customer communications: SE/CS issued incident summaries to affected customers and offered credits; proactive check-ins scheduled for tenant owners.

Why this was unique: Previous reserved-pool incidents typically involved autoscaler headroom misestimation or allocator fragmentation. This incident stemmed from a thin timing race in the token lease lifecycle combined with conservative autoscaler gating, producing a denial mode despite available hardware capacity. That coupling was not covered by earlier test harnesses, hence new chaos tests and TTL-specific observability were added.

Status: Fixes merged and rolled out to all regions. Monitoring graphs remain within normal baselines for 7+ days. Customer tickets closed with follow-up checks scheduled.
